description: NL4SMT benchmark dataset with 25 problems across arithmetic, boolean, optimization, CP, mixed, quantifiers, string, and bitvector categories.

problems.nl: x is an integer. x is greater than 5 and less than 20.
a and b are integers. The sum of a and b equals 100. a is at least 30. b is positive.
m and n are integers. m is exactly 7. n is the product of m and 3.
p, q, r are integers. p plus q plus r equals 30. p is less than q. q is less than r. p is at least 1.
x is an even integer between 2 and 20 inclusive.
a and b are positive integers. a divided by b equals 3 with remainder 1.
p and q are booleans. p implies q. q is false.
x, y, z are boolean variables. At least two of them must be true.
a and b are booleans. a is true if and only if b is true.
p, q, r are booleans. If p is true then both q and r must be true. Otherwise at least one of q or r is false.
x is a boolean. x is not false.
u and v are non-negative integers. u plus v is at most 50. Maximize u.
cost and quality are real variables. cost is at least 1.0. quality equals 10 minus cost. Minimize cost.
x is an integer between 0 and 100. Minimize x squared.
a, b, c are non-negative integers. a plus b plus c equals 30. Maximize the product of a and b.
We have 4 tasks T0, T1, T2, T3. Each task duration is an integer between 1 and 5. All tasks must have different durations.
Array B contains 3 integers. The elements must be in strictly increasing order. Each element is between 1 and 10.
Three workers W1, W2, W3 each choose a shift from 1 to 3. All workers must choose different shifts.
x, y, z are integers from 1 to 10. They must be in non-decreasing order.
i is an integer. r is a real. i is greater than 0. r equals i plus 0.5. If i is even then r is greater than 2.0.
n is a positive integer. A1, A2, A3 are positive integers. All A values are different. Their sum is at most 100.
x is a boolean. y is an integer. If x is true then y is greater than 10. Otherwise y is less than 0.
a and b are integers. c is a real. a is at least 1. b is at least 1. c equals a divided by b. c is less than 1.0.
For all integers x, if x is greater than 0 then x plus 1 is greater than x.
problems.note: Quantifiers require special handling; this is a placeholder.

problems.nl: s is a string. t is a string. s equals t.
x is an integer between 0 and 255. x is greater than 100.
x, y, z are integers. x plus y equals z. x is 5. y is 7.
a, b, c are booleans. a and b and c are all true.
x is an integer between 1 and 10. Minimize x.
x and y are integers from 1 to 5. x and y must be different.
n is an integer. b is a boolean. b is true if and only if n is greater than 10.

We have 3 jobs J1, J2, J3 and 2 machines M1, M2. Each job must be assigned to exactly one machine. J1 takes 2 hours, J2 takes 3 hours, J3 takes 4 hours. Each machine can handle at most 5 hours total. Minimize the makespan (maximum load across machines).

We have 4 nodes A, B, C, D. Each node must be colored with 1, 2, or 3. Adjacent nodes cannot share the same color. A is adjacent to B and C. B is adjacent to A, C, and D. C is adjacent to A, B, and D. D is adjacent to B and C.

A 4x4 Sudoku grid. Each cell Cij (i,j from 1 to 4) contains a digit 1 to 4. Each row must contain all different digits. Each column must contain all different digits. Each 2x2 subgrid must contain all different digits. Cell C11 is 1. Cell C23 is 3.
We have 4 items with values 10, 20, 15, 25 and weights 2, 3, 4, 5. The knapsack capacity is 8. Each item can be taken at most once. Maximize total value without exceeding capacity.

We have 5 tasks T1 through T5. Each task has a duration: T1=2, T2=3, T3=1, T4=4, T5=2. We need to schedule them in a sequence. The start time of each task equals the end time of the previous task. All tasks must finish by time 15. Minimize the total completion time.
We have an array A of size 5. Index i is an integer. We access A[i]. The index i must be at least 0 and less than 5. All elements of A are non-negative. The sum of all elements is at most 100.
A half adder has inputs A and B, outputs S (sum) and C (carry). S is true if exactly one of A or B is true. C is true if both A and B are true. A and B are boolean inputs.

3 students S1, S2, S3 must choose one project each from 3 projects P1, P2, P3. Each project can be chosen by at most 2 students. S1 prefers P1 or P2. S2 prefers P2 or P3. S3 prefers P1 or P3. Maximize the number of students who get their preferred project.

A 3-digit lock code ABC where A, B, C are digits 0-9. The first digit A is odd. The sum of all three digits is 15. The second digit B is greater than the first digit A. The third digit C is the sum of A and B.

A factory produces two products X and Y. Each unit of X requires 2 hours of labor and 3 units of raw material. Each unit of Y requires 4 hours of labor and 1 unit of raw material. Total labor available is 40 hours. Total raw material available is 30 units. Profit per unit of X is 50 dollars and per unit of Y is 40 dollars. Maximize total profit.

We have 4 cities connected by roads: 1-2 (distance 10), 1-3 (distance 15), 2-3 (distance 20), 2-4 (distance 25), 3-4 (distance 30). Find the shortest path from city 1 to city 4. Let Xij be 1 if road i-j is used, 0 otherwise. The total distance is the sum of Xij times road distances.

Three events E1, E2, E3 have start times T1, T2, T3. E1 must happen before E2. E2 must happen at least 5 units after E1. E3 must happen after E2. All events must start between time 0 and time 100. Minimize T3.

Place 4 queens on a 4x4 chessboard so that no two queens threaten each other. Let Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 be the row positions of queens in columns 1, 2, 3, 4 respectively. Each queen must be in a different row. No two queens can be on the same diagonal.
A 3x3 magic square using digits 1 through 9 exactly once. The sum of each row, each column, and both main diagonals must equal 15. Cell Cij is in row i, column j.
Solve the cryptarithmetic puzzle SEND + MORE = MONEY. Each letter S, E, N, D, M, O, R, Y represents a unique digit 0-9. M must not be 0. S must not be 0.

3 jobs must be processed on 2 machines. Job 1 takes 2 hours on machine A and 3 hours on machine B. Job 2 takes 4 hours on machine A and 1 hour on machine B. Job 3 takes 3 hours on machine A and 2 hours on machine B. Each machine can only process one job at a time. Jobs must complete machine A before starting machine B. Minimize the total completion time (makespan).

6 golfers G1-G6 play in 2 groups of 3 for 2 weeks. Each week, every golfer is in exactly one group. No two golfers can be in the same group more than once across all weeks. Let Xgw be the group number (1 or 2) for golfer g in week w.
